name: US Presidents
description: Famous firsts, wartime leaders, vice presidents and the stories behind the office.
question: {prompt}

cards.prompt: Who was the first president of the United States?
cards.fact: Washington took the oath of office in New York City in 1789.

cards.prompt: Which president received the vote of every elector in both of his elections?
cards.fact: No other president has been chosen unanimously by the Electoral College.

cards.prompt: Who was the first president to live in the White House?
cards.fact: Adams moved into the still-unfinished building in November 1800.

cards.prompt: Which future president was the principal author of the Declaration of Independence?
cards.fact: Jefferson and John Adams both died on the same day: July 4, 1826, the Declaration's 50th anniversary.

cards.prompt: Which president bought the Louisiana Territory from France in 1803?
cards.fact: The Louisiana Purchase roughly doubled the size of the United States.

cards.prompt: Which "Father of the Constitution" became the 4th president?
cards.fact: Madison also drafted the Bill of Rights.

cards.prompt: Which president's 1823 doctrine warned European powers against new colonies in the Americas?
cards.fact: The Monroe Doctrine shaped US foreign policy for more than a century.

cards.prompt: Who was the 6th president, the son of the 2nd?
cards.fact: After his presidency he served 17 years in the House of Representatives.

cards.prompt: Which president has appeared on the $20 bill since 1928?
cards.fact: Grant is on the $50 and Lincoln on the $5.

cards.prompt: Which president died just 31 days after taking office in 1841?
cards.fact: Harrison gave the longest inaugural address on record, in cold, wet weather.

cards.prompt: Who was the 16th president?
cards.fact: Lincoln led the Union through the Civil War and issued the Emancipation Proclamation.

cards.prompt: Who assassinated Abraham Lincoln?
cards.fact: Booth, a well-known actor, shot Lincoln at Ford's Theatre in April 1865.

cards.prompt: Which president, impeached in 1868, was the first to be impeached?
cards.fact: The Senate fell one vote short of removing him from office.

cards.prompt: Which Union general of the Civil War became the 18th president?
cards.fact: Grant accepted Robert E. Lee's surrender at Appomattox in 1865.

cards.prompt: Which 19th-century president served two non-consecutive terms?
cards.fact: Cleveland was the 22nd and the 24th president; Benjamin Harrison served in between.

cards.prompt: The teddy bear is named after which president?
cards.fact: Roosevelt refused to shoot a captive bear on a 1902 hunting trip, inspiring the toy.

cards.prompt: Which president later became Chief Justice of the United States?
cards.fact: Taft is the only person to have held both offices.

cards.prompt: Which president was elected to four terms?
cards.fact: Roosevelt died in April 1945, early in his fourth term.

cards.prompt: Who said "The only thing we have to fear is fear itself" in his first inaugural address?
cards.fact: He spoke in March 1933, at the depth of the Great Depression.

cards.prompt: Which amendment, ratified in 1951, limits presidents to two elected terms?
cards.fact: The limit was a response to Franklin Roosevelt's four election wins.

cards.prompt: Which president authorized the atomic bombings of Japan in 1945?
cards.fact: Truman had been vice president for less than three months when Roosevelt died.

cards.prompt: Which Supreme Allied Commander in World War II became the 34th president?
cards.fact: Eisenhower directed the D-Day landings in Normandy in 1944.

cards.prompt: Who was the youngest person ever elected president, at 43?
cards.fact: Theodore Roosevelt was younger, at 42, but he took office on McKinley's death rather than by election.

cards.prompt: Which president was assassinated in Dallas in 1963?
cards.fact: Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson was sworn in aboard Air Force One the same day.

cards.prompt: Which president resigned in 1974 over the Watergate scandal?
cards.fact: Nixon is the only president to have resigned from office.

cards.prompt: Which president was never elected either president or vice president?
cards.fact: Ford was appointed vice president in 1973 and succeeded Nixon in 1974.

cards.prompt: Which former president won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2002?
cards.fact: Carter was honoured for decades of work on peace, human rights and health after leaving office.

cards.prompt: Which president was a Hollywood film actor before entering politics?
cards.fact: Reagan was also governor of California before becoming president.

cards.prompt: Which 41st president was the father of the 43rd?
cards.fact: Only John Adams and John Quincy Adams had done it before.

cards.prompt: Which president was impeached by the House in 1998?
cards.fact: The Senate acquitted Clinton in February 1999.

cards.prompt: Which president was born in Hawaii?
cards.fact: Obama was born in Honolulu in 1961, two years after Hawaii became a state.

cards.prompt: Who was Barack Obama's vice president?
cards.fact: Biden served as vice president for both of Obama's terms, 2009–2017.

cards.prompt: Who was George W. Bush's vice president?
cards.fact: Cheney had earlier served as Secretary of Defense under George H. W. Bush.

cards.prompt: Who was Bill Clinton's vice president?
cards.fact: Gore later won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2007 for his work on climate change.

cards.prompt: How many years is one presidential term?
cards.fact: Senators serve six-year terms and members of the House two.
